page.title: wrenlight Perch — Two-Year Battery Camera & Loft Module

sections.heading: The price of waking up
text: Perch is wrenlight's ultra-low-power outdoor camera: two AA lithium cells, a two-year battery contract, and a wall-powered sync module — the **Loft** — that owns everything expensive. The camera sleeps at *4 µA* behind a PIR gate; a qualified event records a short clip and ships it over **TwigLink**, wrenlight's proprietary *908 MHz* sub-GHz link, to the Loft, which buffers and uploads over house Wi-Fi. Every design decision is an entry in one account book: *3300 mAh* over *730 days* is a daily allowance of *4.5 mAh*, and every wake-up is billed against it.
bullets: **Perch camera** — a dual-chip split: **Twig (WL-LP1)**, an always-on Cortex-M0+ at *4 µA* sleep that owns the PIR analog front end, the thermistor, the TwigLink radio MAC, and the power rail of its big sibling; **Bough (WL-AP4)**, a 1080p video SoC with a *400 ms* boot from retained RAM and *64 MB* of staging flash (about 3 clips), plus an 850 nm IR illuminator — no spotlight.
Power: 2× AA lithium (Li-FeS₂) primary cells in series — *3300 mAh* at *3 V*; alkaline fits the holder but voids the two-year math.
**TwigLink radio** — *908.4 MHz* FSK, *500 kbps*, AES-CCM-128, star topology; every camera is a leaf of exactly one Loft.
**Perch Loft** — wall-powered; a Wi-Fi SoC plus the WL-C2 TwigLink concentrator, a *32 GB* eMMC store-and-forward buffer, USB-A for a local archive drive, and it serves up to *10* cameras.
**Abacus** folds wake receipts into a per-camera forecast and raises the *months left* number the app shows.
The **PIR** front end trips and wakes **Twig** out of its *4 µA* sleep.
**Twig** runs an *800 ms* qualification pass at *2 mA* — PIR pulse shape plus lux check — and a rejected trip (heat shimmer, headlights) goes back to sleep having spent *0.0004 battery-days*.
On a qualified trip, **Twig** raises **Bough**'s power rail; **Bough** boots from retained RAM in *400 ms* at *120 mA*.
**Bough** records a *12 s* clip at *180 mA* — night adds *60 mA* of IR — into staging flash.
*In parallel* **Twig** opens a TwigLink session to the **Loft** with an event pre-notice (camera, timestamp, estimated size).
**Bough** hands the *2.4 MB* encoded clip to **Twig**, and the radio ships it in *8 s* at *45 mA*.
The **Loft** acks the final chunk; **Twig** drops **Bough**'s rail and the camera is back at *4 µA*.
**Twig** appends a wake receipt to its ledger: *0.91 mAh* total, or *0.20 battery-days* — one night event costs *a fifth of a day's allowance*.
The **Loft** forwards the receipt with the clip manifest to **Abacus**.
**Abacus** refolds the forecast — *five* night events a day spends the whole allowance, so today's *eleven* trims the display from *24* to *22* months — and the app graph updates.

**Failure mode — battery low:** staged degradation — at *20%* live view is disabled, at *8%* clips cap at *5 s* and check-ins go daily, at *3%* the camera sends PIR text events only — *a last-gasp doorbell, not a camera*.

sections.heading: A leash made of sub-GHz
text: **Roost** is the device registry and session service: each Loft holds one outbound persistent TLS channel to it, and it tracks per-camera supervision state; **Flitter** fans alerts out as a push. The TwigLink leash between **Twig** and the **Loft** is not persistent — it is a periodic check-in with a retry-and-backoff ladder, and going quiet for too long trips a supervision alarm.
bullets: Every *60 minutes* **Twig** wakes the radio for a *200 ms* check-in: sequence number, battery voltage, temperature, last RSSI.

The **Loft** acks with a clock sync and pending flags — `settings changed`, `arm/disarm`, `firmware offer`. **Molt** (firmware staging) is the service behind the `firmware offer` flag: it *trickles* camera images over TwigLink in the supervision windows, so a sleeping camera never pays for a long download.
On a missed ack **Twig** retries at *+2 s*, *+8 s*, and *+30 s*, hopping channels each attempt.
Still unheard, **Twig** enters backoff — a check-in every *5 minutes* — while PIR rules stay armed locally and new clips park in the *64 MB* staging flash.
After *two* silent check-in windows the **Loft** marks the camera `UNSUPERVISED` and reports it to **Roost**.
**Roost** has **Flitter** push *"Front gate unreachable since 14:20."*
When the link returns, **Twig**'s check-in carries `missed=7, staged=2`, and the **Loft** pulls both staged clips.
The **Loft** clears the supervision alarm through **Roost** and logs the RSSI history for the app's *placement advice*.

**Failure mode — Loft loses power:** cameras stay armed on local rules, stage up to *3* clips in flash, and burn extra battery on retry backoff; **Roost** marks the site offline after *5* missed Loft heartbeats and pushes an outage alert. This is a site-wide failure, distinct from a single camera going `UNSUPERVISED` above.
**Failure mode — RF interference on 908 MHz:** per-attempt channel hopping comes first, as above; if the noise floor stays high, the **Loft** raises an RF-environment alert with the RSSI history.

sections.heading: The module carries it home
text: **Granary** is the clip object store for cloud-plan homes; it indexes USB-archive manifests for local-only homes *without holding their video*. Cameras never speak Wi-Fi at all — the **Loft** is the only hop onto the house network, so the radio link and the Wi-Fi uplink can fail independently.
bullets: **Twig** streams the clip as *1 KB* sequenced TwigLink chunks, each sealed with AES-CCM.
The **Loft** writes chunks straight into its eMMC store-and-forward queue and acks with a window credit.
Lost chunks are re-requested by NACK bitmap — *at most three* repair rounds, because retries bill the camera's battery, not the Loft's wall power.
The **Loft** verifies the final MIC and acks `END`: responsibility transfers, and the camera is released to sleep.
The **Loft** assembles the clip, computes its digest, and enqueues an upload manifest for **Granary**.
The **Loft** uploads over house Wi-Fi TLS; on success the queue entry flips to `uploaded`.
**Granary** triggers **Flitter**, and the push lands with a thumbnail.
If Wi-Fi is down the queue simply holds — *32 GB* is about *three weeks* of clips — and drains oldest-first on return; USB-archive homes *skip the cloud leg entirely*.
**Failure mode — house Wi-Fi drops:** cameras are unaffected (*they never speak Wi-Fi*); the **Loft** keeps taking clips into eMMC and drains the queue on return; pushes arrive late.
**Failure mode — cloud down:** the **Loft** records and buffers as normal; USB-archive homes don't notice; cloud-plan homes see clips arrive in a burst afterward.

sections.heading: Twenty-four below
text: Cold is the other side of Perch's battery math. **Sunrail** is the optional solar mount: a small panel plus a Li-ion buffer cell that *trickles* the AA rail, gated by a temperature-aware charge controller.
bullets: An *hourly* check-in reports the thermistor at *−24 °C*.
The **Loft**'s next ack sets the camera's cold profile.
**Twig** applies the limits: IR illuminator capped at *50%*, clip length capped *12 s → 8 s*, live view refused below *−30 °C*.

The battery gauge switches models: Li-FeS₂ still delivers at *−24 °C* but sags under IR load, so **Twig** reads voltage under a known load and corrects along the temperature curve instead of trusting open-circuit volts.
Qualification thresholds tighten — warm bodies against cold air trip the PIR harder, and small wildlife would otherwise wake **Bough** all night.
On **Sunrail** mounts the charge controller suspends Li-ion charging below *0 °C* (plating risk) and reports `charge_suspended`; the panel still offsets daytime supervision draw.
**Abacus** prices the cold in: *"at −20 °C nightly, forecast 24 → 19 months."*
If the discharge curve says alkaline, the app warns: *months not years*, and dead below *−10 °C* — lithium cells are *a requirement, not a suggestion*.
**Failure mode — alkaline cells installed:** detected by discharge curve; the two-year contract is voided in the app copy and cold limits engage at *−10 °C* instead of *−30 °C*.
